what: Build Check Part 1 (ROC Operations Manual §14.2A): every source the Source Register lists for a finding was reopened on 16 October 2026 and each recorded quotation looked for on its page. 'also_says' lists further sentences the checkers reported on the same pages; some are marked by the checkers as paraphrases and are not relied on.

checks.recorded: "Zones 2-4 [heading] ... Zones 5-6 [heading] ... Zones 7-9 [heading]"
checks.page_wording: Zones 2-4 / Zones 5-6 / Zones 7-9
checks.note: Page has the three zone headings and does not say whether zones are Canadian or USDA. No organisation name or date shown on the fetched text.

checks.recorded: "Tender roses (Hybrid Teas, Floribundas, Austins and Grandifloras) require layers of winter protection."
checks.page_wording: Tender roses (Hybrid Teas, Floribundas, Austins and Grandifloras) require layers of winter protection.
checks.note: Canadian Rose Society page; place not stated beyond a Coastal B.C. mention and Chinook winds. 'Across much of Canada' is an inference from the zone bands, not stated.

checks.recorded: "Otherwise, winter protection is not usually necessary in Coastal B.C"
checks.page_wording: Otherwise, winter protection is not usually necessary in Coastal B.C
checks.note: Says coastal B.C. usually needs no winter protection; the 'except tender or newly planted roses in extreme cold' part rests on the word 'Otherwise' and the preceding sentence, which was not returned verbatim.

checks.recorded: "In the spring, when the bush begins to leaf out again, any winter kill can be removed and the bush shaped if necessary."
checks.page_wording: In the spring, when the bush begins to leaf out again, any winter kill can be removed
checks.note: Same sense; the tail 'and the bush shaped if necessary' was not returned by WebFetch. No month given. Zone 2-4 attribution to this sentence was not separately shown.

checks.recorded: "Cut canes back to about 70cm to 1m (28-40 in) to prevent them whipping about in the wind."
checks.page_wording: Cut canes back to about 70cm to 1m (28-40 in) to prevent them whipping about in the wind.
checks.note: Canadian Rose Society; zone band for this sentence not shown in the returned text.

checks.recorded: "Around Thanksgiving cut canes back to about 70cm (28 in) and defoliate them."
checks.page_wording: Around Thanksgiving cut canes back to about 70cm (28 in) and defoliate them.
checks.note: Page says tender roses in Zones 2-4 are cut back and defoliated around Thanksgiving (Canadian Thanksgiving, second Monday of October); winter-hardy roses are not cut back in fall.

checks.recorded: "Remove all dead leaves and any clippings from the bed."
checks.page_wording: Remove all dead leaves and any clippings from the bed.
checks.note: Canadian Rose Society, in the winter-preparation context. The finding says 'debris'; page says 'clippings'. No month given.

checks.recorded: "When the ground is at least partially frozen, place a collar around each bush"
checks.page_wording: When the ground is at least partially frozen, place a collar around each bush and fill with dry soil and peat moss.
checks.note: Protection tied to ground freezing, not a date. 'After hard frosts' is not in the returned text. Applies to the cold-zone (2-4) method.

contradictions: Winter-hardy roses should not be cut back in fall; only tender roses are cut at Thanksgiving.
Page says ALL newly planted roses in Zones 5-6 should get some winter protection the first winter or two.

also_says.quote: Note that ALL newly planted roses in Zones 5-6 should receive some winter protection the first winter or two
also_says.note: Zones 5-6; no month; Canadian Rose Society

also_says.quote: Covering the bushes in Zones 2-4 is meant to keep them frozen until spring (paraphrase from WebFetch, not verbatim)
also_says.note: Zones 2-4, even where Chinook winds are common

checks.note: Canadian Rose Society, no place or band stated; forsythia is given as an alternative to April.

checks.recorded: "usually April or when the forsythia is in bloom in your area"
